findings.reason: callable.ts:63 adds `readonly hostContext?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined` to RuntimeContextLike, while runtime.ts declares it required and context.ts:314 always defaults it to {}. Every new test casts `(ctx as RuntimeContext)` to reach it. This is an API-typing point and nothing breaks at runtime, so P1's medium is lowered to low.
findings.claim: The host-function ctx type (RuntimeContextLike) declares hostContext as optional, even though the runtime always sets it, so extension authors have to cast or null-check.
findings.evidence: `CallableFn` receives `ctx: RuntimeContextLike`, which declares `readonly hostContext?: Record<string, unknown> | undefined`, while `RuntimeContext` declares `readonly hostContext: Record<string, unknown>` (types/runtime.ts:174). Every new test has to write `(ctx as RuntimeContext).hostContext` to reach it without a null check (host-context.test.ts lines 55, 85, 113, 138, 170).

members.claim: `CallableFn` gives host functions a `ctx` of type `RuntimeContextLike`, and there `hostContext` is optional (`Record<string, unknown> | undefined`). The runtime always sets it to an object, but extension authors can't see that from the type. They have to cast to `RuntimeContext`, as every new test does with `(ctx as RuntimeContext).hostContext`, or add pointless `?.` checks. That undercuts the stated goal of letting extensions use this bag at call time. Make it non-optional here (`readonly hostContext: Record<string, unknown>`) to match `RuntimeContext`.

findings.reason: context.ts:314 stores `options.hostContext ?? {}` as-is, and createChildContext copies `parent.hostContext`. The test asserts identity with the host's object. The sharing appears intended (functions and objects are passed to extensions), so this is an undocumented design point rather than a defect, and it stays low.
findings.claim: hostContext is stored by reference, not copied or frozen, and shared with every child context, so any extension can mutate it and the change is undocumented.
findings.evidence: `hostContext: options.hostContext ?? {}` stores the caller's object as-is, and `createChildContext` copies the same reference (`hostContext: parent.hostContext`). The test 'child context shares same hostContext reference as parent' asserts `refs[0]` is `sharedContext`. The type is `Record<string, unknown>`; the `readonly` applies only to the property, not to the object's contents.

members.claim: The host's `hostContext` object is passed by reference and is not frozen, so any extension or host function can add, replace or delete entries. Those changes are seen by every other extension in the run and by the host's original object. The change does not document this sharing.

members.claim: The context stores the host's object by reference with no copy or freeze, and every child context shares that same reference. Any extension or host function can mutate it, and the change is visible to all later calls in the run. If the host reuses the same options object across `execute()` calls, the changes also carry over into other runs and sessions. If shared mutable state isn't intended, freeze or shallow-copy the object. Either way, document the sharing semantics.

findings.evidence: The 'child context propagation' test runs a conditional branch, which may not actually create a child context through `createChildContext`. Add a test that calls the host function from inside a closure body or a loop, so the `createChildContext` path is really covered.
